newsitem.title: YEMEN: Freed Polish hostages arrive at Sanaa embassy.
newsitem.headline: Freed Polish hostages arrive at Sanaa embassy.

text.p: Five Polish tourists held hostage by Yemeni tribesmen since last week were released by their abductors on Wednesday and driven to the Polish embassy in Sanaa, a senior diplomat said.
"The five Poles arrived at the embassy, they are in good physical and mental condition," Poland's Ambassador to Sanaa Krzysztof Supravicz told Reuters.
Asked whether the freed hostages will leave Yemen soon, Supravicz said: "This is my presumption."
He refused to give the names of tourists.
An official Yemeni source said earlier on Wednesday that the hostages had been released and were proceeding to the capital Sanaa in a heavily guarded convoy.

A Polish diplomat said earlier that the crisis neared its end after Yemen had given written assurances to the abductors that it would not prosecute them for the kidnapping and attacking security forces who tried to inrtevene, but Yemeni officials declined to confirm these reports.

The tourists -- three men and two women between the ages of 50 and 64 -- were kidnapped on their way to archaeological sites in western Yemen last week. It was the second abduction of European holidaymakers within a month.
The tourists were abducted by members of the Al al-Masni tribe in the Khawlan area, about 65-km (40-miles) east of the capital Sanaa.
On Friday, the tribesmen fired rocket-propelled grenades at military forces who had surrounded them, killing three soldiers and wounding five.
A tribal source in Khawlan said that security forces were still beseiging the area where the hostages had been held and are demanding unconditional surrender of the kidnappers.
Asked about assurances given to the kidnappers he said: "The (Yemeni) government was willing to do anything to end the crisis."
Yemeni authorities on December 19 freed five Dutch tourists who were abducted and briefly held by tribesmen while touring an area 240 km (150 miles) north of Sanaa.

In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political.
